episodes.178794: The combination of a strong upper ridge over the region which provided for much above normal temperatures across the area, and an easterly flow over central California  provided for some mid and upper level moisture to stream into the area. With moisture and instability sufficient for convection to take place, scattered thunderstorms broke out during the afternoon over the Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains as well as across the Kern County Deserts. One thunderstorm in the desert produced heavy rainfall which resulted in debris flow flooding over a portion of U.S. 395 near Randsburg.
episodes.178846: A moist, backdoor cold front that moved west through the Rio Grande Valley early on May 21, 2023 provided lift for afternoon showers and thunderstorms. A severe thunderstorm moved southeast from the Albuquerque westside and produced quarter size hail at the Rio Grande Nature Center.
episodes.178953: Accelerated snowmelt from a near-record snowpack due to above normal temperatures produced high and fast flow on the Colorado River. One such area was Glenwood Canyon, where an individual drowned in a rafting accident.
episodes.178955: Accelerated snowmelt from a near-record snowpack due to above normal temperatures and precipitation produced high and fast flow on drainages in Delta and Garfield counties. As a result, flooding compromised various low-lying recreational trails.
episodes.178967: As low pressure and its associated warm front moved northward into southern New England on the 20th, a low level jet helped produce heavy rainfall across the region.  A cold front moved across eastern MA after midnight on the 21st, bringing an end to the rain.  Rainfall amounts generally ranged from 1.5 to 3.0 inches across southern New England, except 3.0 to 4.0 inches in Rhode Island.
episodes.179448: Thunderstorms developed across western Montana ahead of an approaching trough. High amounts of atmospheric moisture and slow storm motion contributed to a flash flood threat, especially over recent burn scars. A few storms produced quarter size hail.
episodes.180277: A surface front settled southward across NE FL in the evening. This feature combined with convergence near the inland advancing east coast sea breeze over a moist and unstable low level airmass triggered a few strong to severe storms.
episodes.180315: Moist, convergent flow over the Atlantic waters lead to the development of a band of showers along the coast of Miami-Dade County on the morning of May 21st.
episodes.180548: Abnormal late-May moisture and weak instability fueled scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Flash flooding and isolated severe weather occurred.
episodes.180549: Abnormal late-May moisture and weak instability fueled scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Several storms produced high winds.
episodes.180711: Continued large-scale troughing and a weak disturbance resulted in strong to severe thunderstorms along the higher terrain of southeast New Mexico.
episodes.180928: Incoming  trough off the Pacific Northwest coast flattened high pressure across the west allowing for increased potential for more widespread showers and thunderstorms through May 21 that continued into the early part of the following week.
episodes.181053: A passing cold front brought more thunderstorms to Eastern Washington. The impacts again included hail, lightning, winds, and flooding from heavy rain.
episodes.181126: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed in the evening of May 20th as a typical summertime day was in place. A cluster of storms formed over St. Tammany Parish and quickly surged southward as a small line segment. The line segment made its way into Lake Borgne where it produced winds over 34 knots before quickly weakening over St. Bernard Parish.
episodes.181303: A slow moving thunderstorm brought heavy rain to the Russell Mountain Burn Scar. The rain and snow melt washed out area road.
episodes.181352: Southwesterly flow aided by an approaching upper level trough facilitated another round of strong diurnal convection during the afternoon hours, starting the central Oregon and along the eastern Mountains before expanding northeastward. Strong to severe T-storms focused in Central Oregon produced up to 1.5 inch hail, strong wind gusts, and heavy downpours that resulted in areas of flash flooding.
episodes.181354: A passing upper-level trough and cold front produced a couple strong to severe T-storms over the eastern mountains aided by diurnal heating. The severe T-storm activity was focused in the Wallowa County area and produced up to 1.5 inch hail, locally gusty winds, and heavy downpours.
episodes.181703: An early monsoonal moisture push occurred during the middle of May across Southern California. The heaviest activity occurred in the High Desert, where several reports of flooding were documented. Hot and humid conditions also occurred region-wide.

events.narrative: Broadcast media partner reported estimated 1 inch hail fell 6 miles SW of Deschutes River Woods at 1738 PDT. A Public report of hail up to 0.88 inches fell 5 miles NNE of Three Rivers.
Report observed while hiking around the Leavenworth area.

Via a public report, 1.5 inch hailstones fell 6 miles SE of Sisters at 1857 PDT, with the public report explaining damage had occurred to a vehicle. Via a public report from social media, hail stones up to 1 inch in size fell 5 miles ESE of Sisters at 1900 PDT.
Public report of traffic driving through several inches of moving water along Highway 395 at Desert Flower Road.
Buoy station at Shell Beach SHBL1 measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 57 mph or 49 knots.
Flash flooding stranded multiple vehicles at and near Artist's Palette.
Report was observed near Chewelah.
California Highway Patrol reported debris flow flooding along U.S. 395 near the intersection of Garlock Rd.
Highway 178 was closed east of Highway 127 due to flooding.
A trained spotter 2 miles W of Madras reported hail stones up to 0.88 inches in size at 2006 PDT.

Via the Jefferson Counties Sheriff's Office social media post, the SW Jordan road leading to the Billy Chinook Lake was closed due to high water and debris from flash flooding. An estimated up to 1.5 inches of rainfall occurred over a 2 hour period within the immediate area, resulting in water draining into a dry waterfall, with the road closure at the bottom of this waterfall.
In Cambridge, Vassar Street, near MIT, was flooded and impassable per campus law enforcement.  Report relayed via amateur radio.
Mesonet station OD191, 2 miles WSW of Mission, reported a wind gust of 62 mph from the outflow boundary of a deteriorating thunderstorm at 2220 PDT.
Highway 95 was flooded north of Goffs Road.

events.narrative: The public reported a waterspout near Miami Beach associated with a weak shower.
Highway 178 was closed at the junction of Highway 127 due to flooding.

Increased snowmelt along the Colorado River led to the closure of Hanging Lake Trail near Glenwood Springs. Water flowed directly down parts of the trail, forcing the closure for approximately a week or so.

Emergency management reported flooding along portions of the North Fork of the Gunnison River near Hotchkiss, mainly in the form of significant erosion of banks along the river. A few cars from a junkyard that was located right against the river bank were taken by the water.
Penny size hail reported near the Rio Grande Nature Center.
There was a public report of quarter size hail near the Rio Grande Nature Center in Albuquerque.

The Colorado River in Glenwood Canyon ran high and fast as a result of accelerated snowmelt. While rafting in Glenwood Canyon, two rafters fell into the river while navigating a rapid and eddy. Both men were pulled from the water and brought back to shore. The rafting party began CPR on the two individuals - one rafter responded, but the other one did not.
Measured severe winds with a vehicle-mounted anemometer.
Observer reported hail on social media. Other hail reports from the storm ranged from 1 to 1.5 inch near Addy.
Wind uprooted large tree.
Hail damaged a sun shade.
Quarter size hail was observed near Doctor's Lake.
An official NWS observation located 2.0 mi SSW of Sun Valley, NV, and the public located in Old Sparks, NV, both reported half inch (dime size) hail.
Report from observers personal weather station located east side of the Pend Oreille River on the mountain. It was reported on social media.
Heavy rain and snow melt led to road washout along the Ball Creek Road. Rain fall amounts were from area observations ranged from 0.3-0.6. It is in the area of the Russell Mountain Burn Scar.
Via a public report, hail up to 0.75 inches fell in North Powder at 1611 PDT.
A deck was damaged by thunderstorm winds in Interlachen. The time of damage was based on radar data. The cost of damage was unknown, but it was estimated for inclusion of the event in Storm Data.
